decision_conditions: The hardstanding and piers by virtue of design, type and materials, would fail to preserve and enhance the character and appearance of the property frontage, the Lakes Estate Conservation Area and the streetscene generally, contrary to Core Strategy (2010) Policies CP30 and CP31, Development Management Document (2014) Policies DMD8, DMD37 and DMD44 as well as having regard to The Lakes Conservation Area Character Appraisal.

The continuation of the loss of front garden soft landscaped area and boundary treatment with hardstanding to facilitate off street car parking would cause harm to the character and appearance of the property frontage, Lakes Conservation Area and the streetscene environment by virtue of the loss of traditional front garden area and boundary treatment, contrary to Core Strategy (2010) Policies CP30 and CP31, Development Management Document (2014) Policies DMD8, DMD37, DMD44 and DMD46 as well as having regard to The Lakes Conservation Area Character Appraisal.

The proposed vehicular access will give rise to conditions prejudicial to the free flow and safety of traffic using the adjoining highway, including pedestrian traffic, and the proposed vehicular access would have a cumulative impact upon kerbside parking. In these respects, the proposal would be contrary to the Council's Revised Technical Footway Guidance 2013, Core Strategy (2010) Policies CP30 and CP31, Development Management Document (2014) Policies DMD37, DMD44 and DMD46 and the aims of the National Planning Policy Framework.
application_type_full: Householder planning & demolition in a conservation area
description: Construction of a hard standing with new tiled footpath, new brick piers and gate in connection with a new vehicular access.
